On 07.10.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.849 of 2016 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 26/06/2019.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 02/02/2016 at about 07:45 p.m., while she was riding motorcycle bearing registration No. KL- 39/E-6586 and when she reached Seaport-Airport road,
motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-32/11-4267 ridden by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked her down, as a result of which she sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/rider filed written statement denying negligence on his part.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the offending motorcycle.
The age, job and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.

Indu Prakash vs Rahul.P.R on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100287963/
2 5.
Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A8 and X1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the offending motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 4,81,661/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a screen printer, was earning 15,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 10,000/- which is on the lower side even going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are no materials on record to prove the income of the claim petitioner.

However, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income of the claim petitioner can be fixed as 10,500/.
Loss of income 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries:
" 1. Type II open distal fracture 1/3rd right ulna and open fracture right radius distal 1/3rd open fracture distal end right radius.
2025
2. Large lacerated wound face.
3. Abrasion wounds face."
She was hospitalized for a period of 11 days.
In all probability, she might have been unable to work for a period of 10 months.
Hence, she can be awarded compensation at the rate of 10,500/-x10 months = 1,05,000/-.

An amount of 30,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal awarded an amount of 10,000/-.
In the facts and circumstances, an amount of 30,000/- as claimed appears to be just and reasonable and the same is awarded under this head.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 49,320/- (total compensation = 5,30,981/-, that is, 4,81,661/- granted by the Tribunal +
49,320/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 122 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The second respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
